newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.

text.p: KUALA LUMPUR, May 14 - Our final estimate on CPO in April shows a slight upward revision of 5,000 tonnes to 728,000 tonnes. Compared to March production rose 45,000 tonnes or 6.6 percent. For the four months ended April production expanded 10.6 percent or 240,000 tonnes to 2.49 million tonnes. The growth is projected to slow down to around three percent in the next eight months. The estimate on end-April stocks of palm oil remains unchanged at 695,000 tones or about 5,000 tonnes more than month earlier.

Stocks of PK/PKO are estimated at around 130,000 tonnes, oil basis. This is also some 5,000 tonnes higher but up 25,000 tonnes when compared to a year ago. Indications of continuing keen competition from Indonesia in the export market may result in a modest rise in palm oil stocks in May and June. Thereafter the projected buildup in stocks will reflect the seasonal rise in production exceeding increases in offtake. In the first-six- months of this year we expect production to trail offtake by 70,000 tonnes.

Palm oil exports are estimated to rise 190,000 tonnes to 3.385 million tonnes with the bulk of the increase accounted by India, The European Union, Indonesia and countries in West Asia. Although offtake is projected to expand 630,000 tonnes to 4.715 million tonnes in the second-half year from 4.085 million tonnes in the first-six months, it is expected to lag behind production by 70,000 tonnes. In other words, we envisage the rise in palm oil stocks in the second-half-year to offset the drawndown in the first-half-year thus resulting in more or less an unchanged stocks situation between end 1997 and 1996.

Palm oil exports are projected to grow to 7.39 million tonnes in 1997 from 7.212 million tonnes last year. The modest increase of about 120,000 tonnes as compared to 700,000 tonnes recorded in 1996 reflected chiefly a slowdown in production supplies as well as a marked reduction in projected CPO imports. This prospective scenario of manageable supplies versus steady demand would provide the basis for the oil palm industry to enjoy another year of good prices. The palm oil market had turned softer in recent days because of a slowdown in new exports sales and a marked drop in shortcovering activities.

Additionally, price of other vegoils also declined. In the last six days the July CPO futures contract lost 45 ringgit or 83 percent of the gains posted in the four weeks ended May 2. It settled at 1,245 ringgit yesterday. The spot May contract fell to 1,275 ringgit, down 59 ringgit from a high of 1,334 ringgit on May 2. July RBDPO/OLN were quoted at $542.5 and $572.5 respectively.
(The opinions expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as necessarily reflecting the views of Reuters).
